parole.testo: Borrowed from Sicilian lignami (“wood”), from Early Medieval Latin lignāmen, derived from Latin lignum. The initial l- was reinterpreted as the Sicilian and/or Maltese definite article. Compare Italian legname.

parole.significato: mountain (large mass of earth and rock)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sicilian muntagna, from Early Medieval Latin montānia, a collective based on Latin montem.
Borrowed from Sicilian parrinu, from Early Medieval Latin patrīnus.

Singularised plural of qalza (“pant leg”), from older Sicilian *calza (“hose, stocking”), from Early Medieval Latin calcea, from Latin calceus (“shoe”). Compare contemporary Sicilian causi, cansi (“trousers”) and, with the original sense and form preserved, Italian calza (“sock, stocking”).
